LESSON: SIGN READING 10.2.2 COMPREHENSION

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade three
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 10
Topic 10.2: Sign Reading 10.2.2 Comprehension
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Sign Reading 10.2.2 Comprehension, part of Strand 10 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade three General.

Key inquiry question: How do we use pictures to make predictions in a story?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Sign Reading 10.2.2 Comprehension together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical thinking and problem solving: as the learner responds to indirect questions using context clues.

● Creativity and imagination: as the learner makes relevant predictions about the story.

Values:
Respect: Open Mindedness as the learner shows positive regard to self and others as they talk about their experiences in relation to the story.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Citizenship: Social cohesion as the learner works together with peers.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner applies comprehension strategies when sign reading texts in other learning areas.

Suggested Learning Resources

Assistive devices fitted with appropriate technology such as Hearing aids and amplifiers, signed audio-visual recordings, print or digital stories, pocket

charts, print and digital flash cards
